passage:
A button fell off Noah's school shirt during class. He put it in his pocket and forgot about it.
At home, he asked his father to sew it back. His father laughed and said, "I can teach you."
Noah thought sewing was too hard, but his father showed him slowly. The first stitch was ugly. The thread became tangled twice. Still, after ten minutes, the button was back on the shirt.
The next week, another student lost a button before a school photo. Noah took out a small sewing kit from his bag and helped him.
Learning one small skill made Noah feel strangely proud. He understood that being independent does not always begin with big things. Sometimes it begins with a button.
